To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The assessment tool is a practical and useful tool for forest departments to monitor and evaluate the implementation and outcomes of devolution policies; 2) The tool is a useful tool for the forest department to learn from local experiences and to adapt their policies to better serve local people; 3) The assessment tool can be applied to other forest departments to assess local outcomes of forest management; and 4) Forest departments can use the assessment tool to assess their devolution policies in other provinces.

a tool developed in collaboration between the Forest Protection Department and the World Resources Institute was used to assess local outcomes of forest management devolution in ten villages in Vietnam, and the tool provided an effective and feasible mechanism to generate information that can contribute to the learning-oriented approach of the Forest Protection Department.

the assessment tool provides forest departments with a practical and feasible way to monitor and evaluate the outcomes of forest devolutions, and that the tool can be applied to assess outcomes at different scales.

the development of tools for assessing local outcomes and impacts of devolution.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(i) forest departments are able to develop assessment tools that can be effectively applied in local settings, and (ii) the assessment tool provides a means for forest departments to develop a learning orientation toward local outcomes of devolutions policies.

the assessment tool is not a static instrument but an evolving process of social inquiry that can help forest departments and other stakeholders to better understand the complex social dynamics of devolution.
forest departments need to be proactive in developing their own assessment tools to monitor and evaluate local outcomes of forest policies.
